clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man with a 30-year history of recurrent toothache presented with a 5-week history of right facial erythema, clustered blisters, and severe pain. He was initially diagnosed with acute periodontitis and herpes zoster (HZ) at a local hospital 4 weeks prior to dermatology clinic referral. Despite treatment with ceftizoxime, metronidazole, acetaminophen, and valacyclovir, his condition worsened and four upper right teeth (teeth 11-17 region) exfoliated 10 days before dermatology clinic admission. Physical examination revealed pigmentation and scars on the right half of the face, complete loss of crowns from teeth 11-17 and 35, gingival recession, and exposure of the alveolar process in the maxillary first quadrant (teeth 11-14). Panoramic radiography and CT imaging showed decreased bone density, poor alveolar socket healing, empty tooth sockets, and periapical cysts. Biopsy of the alveolar process and adjacent mucous membrane revealed fibrinoid necrosis of vascular walls, lumen occlusion, infiltration of histiocytes and neutrophils, and nonvital lamellar bone fragments devoid of osteoblasts and osteocytes surrounded by neutrophils and bacterial aggregates. Debridement was performed, revealing extensive malodorous osteonecrosis in the right maxilla with similar pathological findings and bacterial aggregates in the marrow cavity. Perioperative antiviral (valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 7 days) and antibiotic therapy (cefathiamidine 2 g twice daily for 3 days, then cefuroxime 0.25 g twice daily for 4 days) were administered. Granulation tissue formation was observed 3 weeks after debridement, and at 9-month follow-up, no further tooth exfoliation occurred.
